articles.detail: 5 of 5 cycles completed, avg 12 published per cycle (27 yesterday, 2 of 5 completed)

experiment: Skipped: every goal is met, there are no active or queued experiments and there is no pause gate. This is the first full five-cycle day since 11-13, and one good day is not a reason to change a parameter.
weakestArea: Science is exactly at its floor (5, target 5), from four outlets (Nature, STAT, BBC, Al Jazeera). The US dateline share (23%, cap 25%) has the least headroom of the share targets. Neither one is a miss.
watching: Hormuz: three Tehran-datelined stories across cycles (two tankers mined at 04:51, a projectile strike at 08:40, a third mined tanker at 16:40), plus Iran's winter gas shortage.
Black Sea: drones hit ships off Romania and the Crimean bridge, and a wheat ship capsized off Bulgaria.
Trump, Xi and Putin meet; Trump backs Huang's return and the US closes an AI chip loophole.
Starshield: limits that hobble Ukraine's interceptor drones, and the UK defending its own dependence on it.
Brazil: the Senate passes the fiscal adjustment and the fake-news inquiry closes.
AI governance: California sues OpenAI, ten countries sign the San Francisco supply-chain pact, and the UN presses for rules on killer robots.
coverageGaps: Oceania: 1 story (the Coles cyber attack) after three days at zero.
Science: at the floor with 5 stories; Phys.org and Ars Technica, yesterday's science sources, supplied none today.
context: Throughput is back to 62 articles from 5 of 5 cycles now that the cycle runs on a setup-token after the login expiry of 11-14/15. The 2026-11-13 multi-source watch ended at 35%, met without a change. The three Hormuz stories are separate incidents rather than duplicates (sameEventDuplicates 0), but a rolling single-thread story could serve readers better than one item per incident. Both state-or-advocacy-only stories (the Hormuz projectile from Mehr, the San Francisco AI pact) are labelled in the body.
